title: Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling
abstract: arXiv:2611.26407v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Flow matching is a versatile framework for generative modeling that transports a source distribution to a target data distribution. A key advantage is its flexibility in the choice of source distribution, such as heavy-tailed and multimodal sources. Yet finite-step sampling guarantees for non-Gaussian sources remain limited. We establish a nonasymptotic convergence theory for Euler discretization of flow matching with linear interpolation. Suppose the source distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ has an everywhere positive, continuously differentiable density, finite total variance $\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}$, and an $L$-Lipschitz score. Using the population velocity field and a suitable time grid, this sampler achieves total variation error at most $\varepsilon$ in $\widetilde{O}(Ld\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}/\varepsilon)$ iterations, provided the target distribution satisfies a mild second-moment condition. translated_title: 来自非高斯源的流匹配：高效采样理论
translated_abstract: 流匹配是一种多功能的生成建模框架，它将一个源分布传输至目标数据分布。其关键优势之一在于源分布选择的灵活性，例如可以使用重尾分布和多峰分布作为源。然而，针对非高斯源的有限步采样保证仍然十分有限。本文为采用线性插值的流匹配的欧拉离散化建立了非渐近收敛理论。假设定义在 $\mathbb{R}^d$ 上的源分布具有处处为正、连续可微的密度函数、有限的总方差 $\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}$，以及 $L$-Lipschitz 的得分函数。在使用总体速度场和适当的时间网格时，只要目标分布满足温和的二阶矩条件，该采样器即可在 $\widetilde{O}(Ld\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}/\varepsilon)$ 次迭代内实现至多 $\varepsilon$ 的总变差误差。这些假设涵盖……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文为从非高斯源分布（如重尾和多峰分布）出发的流匹配建立了首个非渐近收敛理论，证明欧拉离散化采样器在温和条件下仅需 $\widetilde{O}(Ld\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}/\varepsilon)$ 次迭代即可达到 $\varepsilon$ 级总变差误差。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes the first non-asymptotic convergence theory for flow matching from non-Gaussian sources (e.g., heavy-tailed and multimodal distributions), proving that Euler discretization achieves $\varepsilon$ total variation error within $\widetilde{O}(Ld\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}/\varepsilon)$ iterations under mild second-moment conditions on the target distribution.
